subject: Interest in Redwood + GitHub integration / Request demo
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@openlib.dev>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interest in Redwood + GitHub integration / Request demo

Hi Camila,

I signed up for Redwood yesterday (really impressive perf numbers on the quickstart!) and I'm the PM on the developer platform team at OpenLib. We're evaluating options for powering a couple of features that will surface model outputs inside GitHub (PR summarization, code search, and an internal assistant).

Two quick questions up front:
- Do you have a GitHub App or Actions-based integration pattern you recommend for embedding inference in CI / PR flows?
- We care a lot about small latency and predictable cost; does Redwood support streaming + function calling for structured outputs?

Would love to get a quick demo next week to walk through integration options and see the private deployment model. Our engineers are particularly interested in whether we can run the inference in our VPC (we're fine with a managed control plane) and how auth would work with GitHub.

Some context: 30-person engineering platform team, heavy use of self-hosted runners in our org, OpenLib is an open-source-first company (repo: https://github.com/openlib/core).

Thanks — can you share availability?

Samira Khan
Product Manager, Developer Platform
OpenLib
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@openlib.dev>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interest in Redwood + GitHub integration / Request demo

Hi Samira — great to meet you (virtually) and thanks for signing up!

High level: yes — we have a few common integration patterns for GitHub workloads (GitHub App + webhooks, Actions-based runners calling our API, and a lightweight SDK for self-hosted runners). We also support streaming responses and function/tool calling in the API so you can build structured PR summaries and batchable analysis pipelines. For private deployments we offer a VPC/on-prem control plane with customer-managed network and KMS/HSM integration.

A couple of quick details that will help us tailor the demo:
- Do you want to see a Hosted API flow (fastest) or Private deployment (VPC) with a GitHub App?
- Are you evaluating for PR-time inference (low latency) or async batch jobs?
- Any compliance constraints (SOC2 / data residency) we should flag?

I looped in Alex (copied) who will coordinate scheduling and run the demo. He can send a calendar invite once we lock time.

I attached a short platform overview that covers deployment modes and integration patterns — we can walk through the architecture during the demo.

Proposed times (PST):
- Thu 10/8 10:00–10:30am
- Thu 10/8 3:00–3:30pm
- Fri 10/9 9:30–10:00am

If none of those work, share your availability and we’ll adapt.

Thanks!

—Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-platform-overview.pdf
From: Samira Khan <samira@openlib.dev>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interest in Redwood + GitHub integration / Request demo

Thanks Camila — this is perfect context.

Answers:
- We'd like to see the Private (VPC) deployment pattern with the GitHub App if possible — repo-level permissions are important for us.
- Primary use case is PR-time inference for summarization (low-latency) but we also have nightly batch jobs for code health metrics.
- SOC2 is on our roadmap but not a blocker for initial evaluation.

Availability: Thu 10/8 3:00–3:30pm PST works for our engineering lead (cc: engineering@openlib.dev).

A couple more engineering notes/questions for the demo:
- Do you have guidance on running inference from self-hosted runners vs. a dedicated inference pool?
- How does token/accounting work if we route through a private deployment (do we still see per-token billing in the console)?

I've attached a short notes file and a link to the repo that shows our current CI hooks — hopefully helpful.

Samira
